title: Adaptive probe suite for multi-profile streaming throughput and p95 regression detection
text:
Adaptive probe suite for multi-profile streaming throughput and p95 regression detection

description:
Problem: Continuous batching and queueing interact unpredictably under mixed tenant workloads (short chat, long generation, streaming) causing opaque p95 regressions and tokens/sec degradations. Objective: Build an adaptive probe suite that (1) exercises multi-profile arrival shapes, (2) tracks tokens/sec and p95 per profile and global, and (3) detects regressions automatically using statistical tests (CUSUM + EWMA thresholds) so we can catch regressions before customer impact.

harness_architecture:
Traffic generator: multi-profile generator that supports weighted mixes of short-chat (<=64 tokens), long-gen (>=1024 tokens), and streaming bursts.
Probe scheduler: adaptive probing that increases probe frequency when variability or tail latency rises.
Measurement collector: per-request metrics (tokens, latency, kv-cache-hit, queue_delay_ms) emitted to Grafana and Prometheus histogram buckets.
Regression engine: offline and online detectors (CUSUM for mean shifts, EWMA for sudden changes) with configurable thresholds per profile.
Isolation harness: ability to pin model variants, enable/disable quantization and preemption to measure interactions.
Artifact links: design doc https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Adaptive+Probe+Suite | dashboard https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/7k8x/perf-probes | prototype PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821

test_plan:
Create synthetic tenant configs: 10 tenants with varying request mixes (90/10 short/long, 50/50, heavy-long-only).
Define arrival distributions: Poisson (lambda tuned), bursty Pareto tails, periodic burst windows to simulate real traffic patterns.
Run baseline: 72-hour steady-state run against runtime-1.21 with current batching and KV cache configs; collect tokens/sec and p95 per-profile.
Introduce controlled perturbations: enable preemption, throttle GPU pool (simulate capacity contention), change batch size heuristics, toggle KV cache hit rates.
Measure: compute p95, p99, tokens/sec, queue_delay_ms, cache_hit_rate. Use CUSUM/EWMA detectors to flag regressions. Store traces for failing windows.
Regression criteria: flag when p95 increases >10% over baseline for a profile for 5 consecutive windows OR tokens/sec drops >15% global for 3 consecutive windows.
Run randomized A/B: compare runtime-1.21 vs candidate changes for 48h to identify regressions ahead of rollout.

acceptance_criteria:
Probe suite can reproduce at least three documented historical regressions from incident logs (validation case).
Automated detector produces <1 false positive per 30d in baseline runs and catches synthetic regressions injected during tests.
Dashboard shows per-profile p95 and tokens/sec with 1m and 5m rollups; alerts wired to Slack and PagerDuty for flagged regressions.
A reproducible runbook and scripts checked into runtime repo (PR merged) and a short how-to in Confluence.

results_summary:
Prototype run (2026-03-09) with 5 tenants, mixed profile (60% short-chat, 30% long-gen, 10% streaming) produced a 12% p95 increase on long-gen when preemption was enabled and KV cache hit < 20%.
Observed tokens/sec volatility: baseline CV=0.08, under bursty arrivals CV=0.21. Continuous batching amplified p95 for long sessions by 18% in peak windows.
Detectors: naive thresholding missed short-lived regressions; CUSUM+EWMA combo caught injected drops within 3 windows and reduced false positives compared to static thresholds.

risks_and_open_questions:
Risk: synthetic mixes may not perfectly mirror customer traffic patterns — plan to onboard one opt-in customer trace anonymized for validation.
Question: trade-off between probe frequency and test cost — need guardrails to avoid excessive load on dedicated pools.
Risk: KV cache instrumentation overhead could impact latency measurements if sampling too aggressive; prefer event-based sampling for full traces.
Question: what alerting SLO should trigger an on-call page vs Slack notice? Proposed: page for global tokens/sec drop >20% for >15m, slack for profile p95 regressions.

next_steps:
Finalize the generator configs and add 10 new tenant mixes (due 2026-03-18).
Merge prototype PR and add CI job that runs a 2-hour smoke probe on PRs touching batching logic (owner: @migs).
Extend detectors to use per-tenant baselining and implement minimum sample size guard in regression engine.
Schedule a cross-team review with PM (Lina Zhou) and Design (Marco Rivera) for dashboard layout and alert UX on 2026-03-16.
Kick off anonymized customer trace import (data team contact: Priya Menon) to validate synthetic mixes.
